newsitem.title: UK: Coffee prices extend a brisk rally.
newsitem.headline: Coffee prices extend a brisk rally.

text.p: World coffee prices rose sharply on Tuesday gaining seven percent in early London trading, buoyed by forecasts of a lower Brazilian crop.
But the market eased later, although it still ended sharply higher, when it emerged that Vietnam would not join any new output curbs agreed among other producer nations.
"The Brazilian news triggered investment fund buying on fears of a shortage of coffee supplies," said a trader.

The head of the primary commodities department of Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry forecast on Monday that the country's 1997/98 crop would reach only 18-20 million 60-kg bags versus 25 million in 1996/97.
Brazil is the biggest coffee grower and exporter.

Robusta coffee on the London futures market jumped seven percent to $1,473 a tonne basis March in early trading, the highest since September last year. The contract ended at $1,460, up six percent on the day.
But Vietnam, a significant Asian producer, said it could not at present afford to join the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).
The ACPC meets in Brazil on Thursday to consider tighter export curbs to lock in the present higher prices.
Elsewhere among commodities on Tuesday, a firmer dollar after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan gave a positive report on the U.S. economy kept the gold market on the defensive.
Gold fixed in London in the afternoon at $354.70 an ounce, just firmer from Monday, but eased later.
The strong dollar was a factor in pushing platinum down to a three-year low at $358.95 an ounce.
Among the industrial metals, zinc was underpinned by a drop in stocks and rallied to a new 23-month high at $1,150 per tonne. Copper ended easier after a rise in warehouse stocks.

London March futures for the world benchmark Brent Blend of crude oil eased as milder weather on both sides of the Atlantic was seen reducing demand for heating fuel. Also, stocks of heating oil are being rebuilt.
Chicago wheat futures eased in follow through to a lower close Monday, traders said.

Pressure remained from an increase this week by the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) in its estimate for the 1996-97 Australian wheat crop. AWB estimated the crop at 23 million tonnes, above the previous estimate for 21.5 million tonnes.
